onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. Near-RT RIC xApps influence resource allocation policies through the E2 interface, and a bug in xApp logic can propagate incorrect scheduling decisions to the O-DU.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC resource management xApp)

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — same as Mild CCI. Severity reflects interference power level at injection time, not a different temporal onset mechanism.
causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. The severity distinction comes from TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not from 3GPP.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — static congestion reflects a sustained traffic overload condition already at saturation level; PRB utilization is high from the start of the anomaly window rather than building up.
causal_mechanism: Static high network congestion occurs when sustained traffic demand exceeds the available radio resources in the cell. PRB utilization in both uplink and downlink reaches saturation (near 100%). With all PRBs allocated, the scheduler cannot serve additional UEs or increase throughput, causing TX_Bytes to plateau and Estimated_UL_Buffer to grow. DL_MCS and UL_MCS may drop as the scheduler is forced to serve cell-edge UEs. Distinguished from Buffer Overflow by the cell-wide PRB saturation pattern versus UE-specific buffer growth.

onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'

causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).

If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. Near-RT RIC xApps influence resource allocation policies through the E2 interface, and a bug in xApp logic can propagate incorrect scheduling decisions to the O-DU.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC resource management xApp)

layer_c_domain_standards.causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'

standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — same as Mild CCI. Severity reflects interference power level at injection time, not a different temporal onset mechanism.
causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. The severity distinction comes from TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not from 3GPP.

onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)

causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. Near-RT RIC xApps influence resource allocation policies through the E2 interface, and a bug in xApp logic can propagate incorrect scheduling decisions to the O-DU.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC resource management xApp)

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).

standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

Defines timing accuracy requirements for logging handover failure events. Note: this clause records handover failures; it does not define A3 event thresholds, hysteresis, or the handover algorithm itself.
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains HANDOVER REQUIRED, HANDOVER REQUEST, Handover Notify, conditional handover (condHandover-r16), handover failure (condHandoverFailure-r16), Handover Failure Log Reporting, Relative Time Stamp Accuracy, N1-to-N1 handover, X2AP handover procedures, and Dual Active Protocol Stack from TS 38.133, TS 38.523, and TS 32.423.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Handover parameter control (A3 event thresholds, hysteresis, time-to-trigger) may be managed by Near-RT RIC xApps via the E2 interface in O-RAN deployments. The KG contains Near-RT RIC traffic steering, cell reselection/handover parameter adjustment, and E2 control procedures. This is an architectural mapping.

onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — static congestion reflects a sustained traffic overload condition already at saturation level; PRB utilization is high from the start of the anomaly window rather than building up.
causal_mechanism: Static high network congestion occurs when sustained traffic demand exceeds the available radio resources in the cell. PRB utilization in both uplink and downlink reaches saturation (near 100%). With all PRBs allocated, the scheduler cannot serve additional UEs or increase throughput, causing TX_Bytes to plateau and Estimated_UL_Buffer to grow. DL_MCS and UL_MCS may drop as the scheduler is forced to serve cell-edge UEs. Distinguished from Buffer Overflow by the cell-wide PRB saturation pattern versus UE-specific buffer growth.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. Near-RT RIC xApps influence resource allocation policies through the E2 interface, and a bug in xApp logic can propagate incorrect scheduling decisions to the O-DU.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC resource management xApp)

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — same as Mild CCI. Severity reflects interference power level at injection time, not a different temporal onset mechanism.
causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. The severity distinction comes from TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not from 3GPP.

_evaluation_note: ground-truth labels may be present in the Layer 2 file but is intentionally excluded from the RCA evidence object. RCA operates on anomaly_type only, as ground truth is unavailable in real deployment.
onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. Near-RT RIC xApps influence resource allocation policies through the E2 interface, and a bug in xApp logic can propagate incorrect scheduling decisions to the O-DU.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC resource management xApp)

standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — same as Mild CCI. Severity reflects interference power level at injection time, not a different temporal onset mechanism.
causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. The severity distinction comes from TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not from 3GPP.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).

onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.

onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through one of three failure modes: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering causing the strict decreasing priority rule to be violated, resulting in lower-priority channels consuming grants ahead of higher-priority ones; (3) Bj state corruption causing the MAC entity to misallocate resources across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values that do not match expected load, with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available and allowed for transmission (unless enhancedSkipUplinkTxDynamic or skipUplinkTxDynamic conditions are met).

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — same as Mild CCI. Severity reflects interference power level at injection time, not a different temporal onset mechanism.
causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. The severity distinction comes from TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not from 3GPP.

onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.
