onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)

onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

layer_c_domain_standards.causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §4.2.1 (BS type 1-C conducted requirement reference points; antenna connector) + TS 38.141-1 §7.2 (Reference sensitivity level)
standards_evidence.clause_text: §4.2.1: 'The conducted requirements for BS type 1-C are specified at the BS antenna connector.' §7.2 defines the reference sensitivity level as the minimum mean power applied to each antenna connector at which the throughput requirement shall be met.
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains AAS BS, antenna array, composite antenna, receiver RF requirements, transmitter characteristics, and OTA co-location requirements from TS 38.141-1 and TS 38.104. onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §6.1.3.1 (Buffer Status Report MAC CEs — Short BSR, Long BSR, Extended BSR, Truncated BSR formats) + TS 38.321 §5.4 (BSR procedure)

standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler responsible for uplink PRB allocation and BSR processing runs in the O-DU. Buffer overflow is a scheduling/resource allocation failure at the O-DU layer.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TS 38.133 §4.3.5 (Relative Time Stamp Accuracy for Radio Link Failure and Handover Failure Log Reporting) + TS 38.331 RRC handover configuration and procedure clauses
standards_evidence.clause_text: TS 38.133 §4.3.5: 'This clause specifies the requirements for Relative Time Stamp Accuracy for Radio Link Failure and Handover Failure Log Reporting.' Defines timing accuracy requirements for logging handover failure events. layer_c_domain_standards.causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)

onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.

standards_evidence.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
standards_evidence.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31) is: exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
standards_evidence.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
standards_evidence.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
standards_evidence.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)

causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.

onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.

onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.

onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.
